This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 438 of Cr.P.C for grant of anticipatory bail relating to Offence No.04/09, dated 4.2.2009, registered at Police Station Economic Offence Wing, District Jabalpur (M.P.) for commission of offences under Section 420,
467, 468, 471, 120-B of IPC and Section 13(1)(d), 13(2) Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Applicant apprehending his arrest has knocked the portal of this Court for grant of anticipatory bail.

2. As per the prosecution story, an FIR was registered against applicant and others alleging that they committed irregularity and embezzled an amount of almost Rs.35,58,707/- in purchase of drum coal tar from Indian Oil Corporation Office, Mathura and for this purpose they prepared forged documents also.
After investigation charge sheet has been filed.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
He is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
In this case, after investigation charge sheet has been filed and during course of investigation, he was not arrested.
He stood retire from the department 10 years back and at present, he is 74 years old.

He apprehends that if he appear before the trial Court,
he may be sent to jail, while he is not required for interrogation or investigation purposes any more.
Learned counsel for the applicant placed reliance on the case of Mahdoom Bava Vs.
Central
Bureau of Investigation
reported in 2023 SCC OnLine SC 299, wherein, in somewhat same facts and scenario, Apex Court has granted anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Therefore, it is prayed that applicant may be released on anticipatory bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for the Economic Offence Wing has opposed grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant but has fairly admitted that after investigation, charge sheet has been filed and in the course of investigation applicant was not arrested.
He has further admitted that now applicant is not required for any investigation or interrogation purpose.
5. In this case, after investigation charge sheet has been filed.
Undoubtedly, applicant is 75 years old man.
He is a retired Government employee.
There is no possibility of his fleeing from justice.

In same facts and situation, Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Mahdoom Bava (supra) observed as under :-
"9.

O n the strength of the aforesaid allegations, which are certainly serious in nature,
the prayer of the appellants for anticipatory bail is opposed vehemently by the learned Additional Solicitor General.
But in our considered view there are at least three factors which tilt the balance in favour of the appellants herein.
They are:-

(i) Admittedly, the CBI did not require the custodial interrogation of the appellants during the period of investigation from 29.06.2019 (date of filing of FIR) till 31.12.2021 (date of filing of the final report).

Therefore, it is difficult to accept the contention that at this stage the custody of the appellants may be required;
(ii) In the reply/counter filed before the High Court, the CBI had taken a categorical stand that the Court had merely issued summons and not warrant for the appearance of the accused.

In the case of Shri Deepak Gupta, CBI had taken a stand before the Special Court that "the presence of the accused is not required for the investigation but it is certainly required for trial" and that therefore he needs to be present.
Therefore, all that the CBI wanted was the presence of the accused before the Trial Court to face trial.

In such circumstances, to oppose the anticipatory bail request at this stage may not be proper; and (iii) All transactions out of which the complaint had arisen, seem to have taken place during the period 2009-2010 to 2012-2013 and all are borne out by records.
When the primary focus is on documentary evidence, we fail to understand as to why the appellants should now be arrested.
10. More importantly, the appellants apprehend arrest, not at the behest of the CBI but at the behest of the Trial Court.

This is for the reason that in some parts of the country, there seems to be a Teerath Prasad Namdeo vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51855322/
2 practice followed by Courts to remand the accused to custody, the moment they appear in response to the summoning order.

entities.text: Teerath Prasad Namdeo vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The correctness of such a practice has to be tested in an appropriate case.

Suffice for the present to note that it is not the CBI which is seeking their custody, but t h e appellants apprehend that they may be remanded to custody by the Trial Court and this is why they seek protection.
We must keep this in mind while deciding the fate of these appeals. "

6. Considering the above submissions put forth by learned counsel for the parties, but without expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which custodial interrogation of the applicant is not warranted as charge sheet has already been filed.
Consequently, this first anticipatory bail application under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of anticipatory bail filed on behalf of applicant stands allowed.

7. It is directed that in the event of arrest/or his first appearance before trial Court applicant - Teerath Prasad Namdeo be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one separate surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Arresting Authority/Trial Court subject to following conditions:-
(i) Applicant shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer;
(ii) In case, applicant is not arrested within a period of 10 days from today, he shall surrender himself before the Trial Court within a period of 10 days from today failing which this order shall become ineffective.
8.

However, it is being made clear that in case of bail jump and in violation of any of conditions imposed herein above, this order shall become ineffective and Trial Court shall be at liberty to proceed against the applicants as per law.
Certified copy as per rules.

(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE mrs. mishra Teerath Prasad Namdeo vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/51855322/
